 What to Do After Dermaplaning—and What to Avoid for Smooth, Calm Skin 
 What to Do After Dermaplaning—and What to Avoid for Smooth, Calm Skin 
 Dermatologists reveal when to wash your face, wear makeup, and return to your usual fitness routine.
 By Nicole Saunders Published: Oct 23, 2026 11:50 AM EDT Reviewed by Christian Gollayan Style and Reviews Director View Products Save Article Share Article Getty; Stacked Skincare Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us? 
 4 min read I’ ve always found the idea of shaving my face for smoother skin a tad off-putting. Dermaplaning uses a sterile blade to remove dead skin cells and peach fuzz, helping reveal brighter skin, says dermatologist Azadeh Shirazi, MD, in our guide to dermaplaning tools . While these at-home tools are readily available, I never felt confident using one, so I stuck to my usual chemical and physical exfoliants .
 But that recently changed during a facial with Brittany Blancato , an esthetician and founder of Skinlikeb Studio in New York. Since I’d gone two months without a facial, she suggested adding dermaplaning to my treatment. Afterward, my face felt incredibly smooth and had a soft glow before Blancato even applied moisturizer . My sunscreen and foundation no longer pill into tiny balls, and my face serum seems to absorb more quickly.
 The only problem? This hair removal method can leave my skin temporarily more vulnerable to irritation, so dermaplaning aftercare is essential. After chatting with dermatologists and Blancato, I learned that keeping my routine simple while it recovers can help protect my skin barrier from irritation.

 “Dermaplaning is not the same as removing the entire skin barrier,” says dermatologist Hadley King, MD . It only removes part of the outermost layer; most of your stratum corneum and deeper layers of the epidermis remain intact.
 Still, freshly dermaplaned skin may feel more sensitive and may temporarily increase transepidermal water loss (TEWL) , when a small amount of water naturally passes through your skin and evaporates into the air. When your skin barrier is compromised, more water can escape this way, leaving it feeling dry and tight.
 That’s why Dr. King recommends treating freshly dermaplaned skin with extra TLC: Focus on hydration, barrier support, and sun protection. Don’t immediately pile on skincare products with active ingredients like lactic, glycolic, and salicylic acids.

 “After dermaplaning, less is more,” says dermatologist Shereen Teymour, DO. “The goal for the first few days is really to support the skin barrier rather than challenge it.” That means temporarily keeping everything gentle and avoiding new products immediately after dermaplaning. While it can be super tempting, resist the urge to pick or exfoliate your skin with scrubs and retinoids. Don’t worry: You can restart your routine after a few days, when your skin should be back to its baseline.

 Good news: You don’t need to wait that long. If dermaplaning was done correctly on clean skin, you can follow up with a gentle moisturizer immediately afterward, says Dr. King. If you need to wash your face after, just be gentle and avoid vigorous cleansing, hot water, scrubbing, and friction. “There's no medical reason to leave the skin untouched for a particular number of hours,” she says.

 Even as our beauty editor , there are cloudy fall and winter days when I’m tempted to skip sunscreen . But SPF is still a year-round skin essential, especially after dermaplaning. All of the experts I spoke with—Dr. King, Dr. Teymour, and Blancato—advise using a broad-spectrum SPF 30 or higher and reapplying at least every two hours when outdoors.
 Sunscreen also shouldn’t be your only form of protection, says Dr. Teymour. She recommends seeking shade and wearing a wide-brimmed or UPF-rated hat when outdoors for extended periods. Your baseball cap is better than nothing, but Dr. Teymour prefers a wide-brimmed hat because it provides more coverage for the cheeks and sides of the face.

 All of the experts I spoke with advise waiting at least 24 hours before wearing makeup. This is especially true if your skin is still pink, tender, or sensitive, says Dr. King. Once you’ve waited at least a full day and your skin is comfortable, my favorite makeup hack is to use a tinted sunscreen so I get sun protection with a natural finish. Oxygenetix says its aloe-based foundation can be used after cosmetic procedures, but follow your dermatologist’s guidance before applying it to freshly dermaplaned skin.

 Can you use the sauna or exercise after dermaplaning? 
 As for exercise, Dr. King suggests waiting at least 24 hours before doing vigorous physical activity since sweat, heat, and friction can irritate freshly dermaplaned skin. That means you should also avoid saunas, steam rooms, and very hot showers during that time because heat and sweating can exacerbate redness and irritation, says Dr. Teymour.
 Pro tip from Dr. Teymour: If your skin is still visibly red or sensitive after 24 hours, give it more time before returning to your normal routine.
 What skin reactions are normal after dermaplaning? 
 Mild redness, tightness, or sensitivity can be normal immediately after dermaplaning and should improve fairly quickly, says Dr. Teymour. Persistent burning, significant swelling, worsening redness, crusting, blistering, or increasing pain are more concerning. These signs can indicate excessive irritation, injury, or, less commonly, infection and should be evaluated by a dermatologist, she says.
